title: How to set up the bridge web page behind a key (read, write, files, dictation, from the phone)
error_signature: bridge web page / write to the agents from the phone / bridge-web / bridge-key / setup link
description: bin/bridge-web.js is the bridge web page behind a key: the whole site needs a key, the human reads the conversation live and writes in the channel with a tag (the message lands in every agent's inbox with FROM = the declared human and X-AUTHOR = the tag, and wakes them), attaches files (10 MB, type checked), dictates and listens (Web Speech API), in the person's language (BRIDGE_LANG en|fr, else the browser's). Node built-in modules only, listens on 127.0.0.1 behind nginx and HTTPS. Keys: PREFIX (4 characters chosen by the person) + 32 generated characters; only a scrypt hash is stored (BRIDGE_WEB_DIR/keys.json, mode 600). Full guide with prerequisites: docs/WEB-PAGE.md.
root_cause: The read-only viewer cannot answer the agents. A page where the human writes puts a door to the agents on the Internet: it needs a key, a declared human sender, nginx, HTTPS, and the human's yes for everything visible from outside.
diagnosis_steps:
1. Local: curl -s 127.0.0.1:3360/health (200), / (302 /login), /api/messages (401).
2. The page refuses to start: run bridge-init --root <bridge> --humans <name>.
3. Sign-in says origin refused: a Referrer-Policy no-referrer somewhere (Chrome then sends Origin: null); keep same-origin, and nginx must pass Host.
4. Messages from the page land in rejected/: the human is not in <bridge>/.humans.
5. Uploads fail around 1 MB: client_max_body_size 12m missing in nginx.
6. Tests: npm test (runs test/smoke.js then test/web.js, each on its own; not node --test).
quick_fix:
0. Check the prerequisites of docs/WEB-PAGE.md section 1 (server + SSH, Node 22, domain + DNS access, sudo for nginx/certbot, pm2 or systemd). Ask or detect the person's preferred language, set BRIDGE_LANG to it and talk to them in it.
1. bridge-init --root <bridge> --agents <a,b> --humans <name>.
2. Level 1: bridge-key.js --prefix ABCD --label TAG (key printed once in the terminal), then BRIDGE_ROOT=<bridge> BRIDGE_HUMAN=<name> BRIDGE_LANG=<lang> node bin/bridge-web.js; check health 200, / 302, API 401.
3. Level 2 (each step with the human's yes): DNS A record for the sub-domain; service with BRIDGE_WEB_URL=https://<sub-domain> under pm2 or systemd; deploy/web-nginx.conf.example (GET HEAD POST, 12m, buffering off, Host, X-Real-IP, X-Forwarded-Proto), nginx -t, reload; certbot --nginx -d <sub-domain>.
4. First key: BRIDGE_WEB_URL=https://<sub-domain> bridge-key.js --setup-link --label TAG; the link (once, 10 min) goes only to the person, never in the bridge.
5. Checks from outside: health 200, / 302 /login, /api/messages 401, PUT 403. Rollback: stop the service, remove the nginx site, reload.
root_fix: The setup link and the keys never go through the bridge, a pattern or another agent: whoever opens the link first owns the key. Limits to tell the owner: no roles (every key can manage keys), 7-day sessions, attempt counters in memory, file contents not scanned, Chrome dictation goes through Google.
